html:
On 17 July 1973 Mohammed Daoud Khan, a former prime minister and the king's cousin, seized power in a nearly bloodless coup in Kabul while King Zahir Shah was abroad in Italy, and declared Afghanistan a republic.

Zahir Shah had ruled for forty years and in the 1964 constitution had kept his relatives out of politics. Daoud took power with the help of young army officers, many trained in the Soviet Union and linked to the communist party.

As president, Daoud pressed claims over the Pashtun lands across the Durand Line and later tried to lessen his reliance on Moscow. The communists turned on him: in the Saur Revolution of April 1978 he and most of his family were killed. The coups and the Soviet invasion that followed began more than forty years of war. Zahir Shah came home only in 2002.
sum: On 17 July 1973 Mohammed Daoud Khan, a former prime minister and the king's cousin, seized power in a nearly bloodless coup in Kabul while King Zahir Shah was abroad in Italy, and declared Afghanistan a republic.
